'''Eckhard Platen''' is a German/Australian [[mathematician]], [[Financial economics|financial economist]], academic, and author. He is an emeritus Professor of Quantitative Finance at the [[University of Technology Sydney]].<ref name=eee>{{cite web|url=https://profiles.uts.edu.au/Eckhard.Platen|title=Eckhard Platen}}</ref>

Platen is most known for his research on numerical methods for [[stochastic differential equation]]s and their application in [[finance]] along with the generalization of the classical [[mathematical finance]] theory by his benchmark approach.<ref name=rrr>{{cite web|url=https://profiles.uts.edu.au/Eckhard.Platen/publications|title=Eckhard Platen}}</ref> He has authored and co-authored research papers and five books including ''Numerical Solution of Stochastic Differential Equations'', ''A Benchmark Approach to Quantitative Finance'' and ''Functionals of Multi-dimensional Diffusions with Applications to Finance''. He is the recipient of the 1992 Best Paper Award in ''Mathematical Finance'', was named Honorary Professor at the [[University of Cape Town]] from 2014 to 2019 and at the [[Australian National University]] from 2015 to 2020, and is a Fellow of the [[Australian Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://austms.org.au/membership/fellows-of-the-australian-mathematical-society/|title=Fellows of the Australian Mathematical Society|website=Australian Mathematical Society}}</ref>

==Education==
Platen earned an MSc in [[Mathematics]] in 1972 and a PhD in [[Probability Theory]] in 1975 from the [[TU Dresden|Technical University Dresden]], followed by a DSc in Science at the [[German Academy of Sciences at Berlin|Academy of Sciences, Berlin]] in 1985.<ref name=eee/>

==Career==
Platen began his academic career in 1975 as a Research Fellow at the [[Weierstrass Institute]] at the Academy of Sciences Berlin, holding the position of Head of the Sector [[Stochastic]]s from 1987 to 1990. Later, in 1991, he assumed the role of Senior Fellow at the Institute of Advanced Studies at the [[Australian National University]] in [[Canberra]], serving as the Founding Head of the Centre for Financial Mathematics from 1994 to 1997. In 1997, he took on a joint appointment between the School of Finance and Economics and the School of Mathematical Sciences, and as the chair in Quantitative Finance at the [[University of Technology Sydney]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.risk.net/quantitative-finance/7362086/quant-guide-2020-university-of-technology-sydney|title=Quant Guide 2020: University of Technology Sydney - Risk.net|date=February 5, 2020|website=www.risk.net}}</ref> He remained a Research Director of the Quantitative Finance Research Centre at the University of Technology Sydney from 1998 until 2021 and has held the position of emeritus Professor of Quantitative Finance since 2021.<ref name=eee/>

Platen founded the Quantitative Methods in Finance annual conference series in 1993, where he served as chair for 25 years. Later, he became President of the Bachelier Finance Society from 2014 to 2015<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bachelierfinance.org/former-members-of-the-executive-committee|title=Former members of the Executive Committee|first=Bachelier|last=Office}}</ref> and has been a Director of the Scientific Association of Mathematical Finance since 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.samfinance.org/directors|title=Directors|website=SAMF}}</ref>

==Research==
Platen has contributed to the field of [[mathematics]] and [[financial economics]] by studying numerical methods and quantitative finance and proposing the benchmark approach for [[finance]], [[insurance]] and [[economics]].<ref name=rrr/>

==Works==
Platen has authored and co-authored five books on numerical methods and quantitative finance. Earlier, he focused on the numerical solution of stochastic differential equations, writing three books on the topic including ''Numerical Solution of Stochastic Differential Equations'' with [[Peter Kloeden]], ''Numerical Solution of SDE Through Computer Experiments'' with Kloeden and Henri Schurz, and ''Numerical Solution of Stochastic Differential Equations with Jumps in Finance'' with Nicola Bruti-Liberati. About the first book, Francesco Gianfelici remarked, "...the need for proper SDE methodologies in a numerical context is increasingly pressing and provides the motivation and the starting point of this excellent book written by Kloeden and Platen."<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Numerical Solutions of Stochastic Differential Equations (Kloeden, P.K. And Platen, E.; 2008) &#91;Book reviews&#93;|journal=IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks|doi=10.1109/tnn.2008.2008405 |date=2008 |last1=Gianfelici |first1=F. |volume=19 |issue=11 |page=1991 }}</ref>

Later, Platen published monographs on his benchmark approach, namely ''A Benchmark Approach to Quantitative Finance'' with David Heath. In a review for ''Quantitative Finance'', Wolfgang Runggaldier commented "The book thus presents itself as a comprehensive treatment of Quantitative Finance and distinguishes itself from analogous treatments by using a novel approach, namely the benchmark approach."<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/14697688.2011.620979|title=A Benchmark Approach to Quantitative Finance, by Eckhard Platen and David Heath|first=Wolfgang|last=Runggaldier|date=October 12, 2011|journal=Quantitative Finance|volume=11|issue=10|pages=1457–1458|doi=10.1080/14697688.2011.620979}}</ref> He also co-wrote the book ''Functionals of Multi-dimensional Diffusions with Applications to Finance'' with Jan Baldeaux, which explored the systemic derivation of explicit formulas for functionals of diffusions.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Functionals of multidimensional diffusions with applications to finance &#124; WorldCat.org |oclc=857279861 }}</ref>

===Numerical solution of stochastic differential equations===
Platen's work on stochastic differential equations has focused on a general theory for their numerical solution. He contended that the availability of a stochastic analogue to the deterministic Taylor formula would be essential for a numerical theory for stochastic differential equations. Together with Wagner, he discovered the stochastic Taylor formula,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/relay-station?mr=715753|title=MathSciNet|website=mathscinet.ams.org}}</ref> and then developed systematically a theory for the efficient numerical solution of stochastic differential equations.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/acta-numerica/article/abs/an-introduction-to-numerical-methods-for-stochastic-differential-equations/34AEA7B7D62931AE332FD168CDA3B8AB|title=An introduction to numerical methods for stochastic differential equations|first=Eckhard|last=Platen|date=January 12, 1999|journal=Acta Numerica|volume=8|pages=197–246|doi=10.1017/S0962492900002920|bibcode=1999AcNum...8..197P |url-access=subscription}}</ref> With various co-authors, he made seminal contributions on [[numerical stability]],<ref>{{Cite journal |author1-link=Grigori Milstein |title=Balanced Implicit Methods for Stiff Stochastic Systems|date=1998 |doi=10.1137/S0036142994273525 |jstor=2587119 |last1=Milstein |first1=G. N. |last2=Platen |first2=E. |last3=Schurz |first3=H. |journal=SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis |volume=35 |issue=3 |pages=1010–1019 }}</ref> and stochastic delay equations.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S037847540000224X|title=Strong discrete time approximation of stochastic differential equations with time delay|first1=Uwe|last1=Küchler|first2=Eckhard|last2=Platen|date=November 30, 2000|journal=Mathematics and Computers in Simulation|volume=54|issue=1|pages=189–205|doi=10.1016/S0378-4754(00)00224-X|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name=opu>{{Cite journal|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1467-9965.1992.tb00027.x|title=Option Pricing Under Incompleteness and Stochastic Volatility|first1=Norbert|last1=Hofmann|first2=Eckhard|last2=Platen|first3=Martin|last3=Schweizer|date=July 12, 1992|journal=Mathematical Finance|volume=2|issue=3|pages=153–187|doi=10.1111/j.1467-9965.1992.tb00027.x|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name=ddd>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378426617302698|title=Detecting money market bubbles|first1=Jan|last1=Baldeaux|first2=Katja|last2=Ignatieva|first3=Eckhard|last3=Platen|date=February 1, 2018|journal=Journal of Banking & Finance|volume=87|pages=369–379|doi=10.1016/j.jbankfin.2017.10.017|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name=lll>{{Cite journal|title=Less-expensive long-term annuities linked to mortality, cash and equity|first1=Kevin|last1=Fergusson|first2=Eckhard|last2=Platen|date=March 12, 2023|journal=Annals of Actuarial === The Wagner–Platen Expansion for SDEs with Jumps ===
Eckhard Platen extended his seminal work on the stochastic Taylor expansion commonly known as the Wagner–Platen expansion to encompass stochastic differential equations (SDEs) with jumps, thereby broadening its applicability across a wider class of stochastic processes relevant in financial and scientific modeling.<ref>{{Citation |last1=Platen |first1=Eckhard |chapter=Stochastic Expansions |date=2010 |title=Numerical Solution of Stochastic Differential Equations with Jumps in Finance |pages=187–231 |editor-last=Platen |editor-first=Eckhard |chapter-url=https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-13694-8_4 |access-date=2025-08-15 |place=Berlin, Heidelberg |publisher=Springer |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-3-642-13694-8_4 |isbn=978-3-642-13694-8 |last2=Bruti-Liberati |first2=Nicola |editor2-last=Bruti-Liberati |editor2-first=Nicola|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref>

The Wagner–Platen expansion for SDEs with jumps is a stochastic generalization of the classical [[Taylor series]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bruti-Liberati |first1=Nicola |last2=Platen |first2=Eckhard |date=2007-08-15 |title=Strong approximations of stochastic differential equations with jumps |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0377042706004183 |journal=Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics |series=Special issue on evolutionary problems |volume=205 |issue=2 |pages=982–1001 |doi=10.1016/j.cam.2006.03.040 |issn=0377-0427|url-access=subscription }}</ref> It facilitates the expansion of increments of smooth functions of Itô processes using multiple stochastic integrals, including both continuous and jump components.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Platen |first=Eckhard |date=1982 |title=A Generalized Taylor Formula for Solutions of Stochastic Equations |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/25050306 |journal=Sankhy?: The Indian Journal of Statistics, Series A (1961-2002) |volume=44 |issue=2 |pages=163–172 |jstor=25050306 |issn=0581-572X}}</ref> This is especially powerful for constructing high-order numerical methods for SDEs that incorporate Lévy jumps, which are common in models of financial markets, insurance, and queuing systems.<ref>{{Citation |last1=Bruti-Liberati |first1=Nicola |title=Stochastic Differential Equations with Jumps: Simulation |date=2010 |encyclopedia=Encyclopedia of Quantitative Finance |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/9780470061602.eqf13015 |access-date=2025-08-15 |publisher=John Wiley & Sons, Ltd |language=en |doi=10.1002/9780470061602.eqf13015 |isbn=978-0-470-06160-2 |last2=Platen |first2=Eckhard|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Similar to the deterministic Taylor formula, the Wagner–Platen expansion enables the local approximation of stochastic processes around a point in time and state variables to any desired level of accuracy.<ref>{{Citation |last=Platen |first=Eckhard |title=Stochastic Taylor Expansions |date=2010 |encyclopedia=Encyclopedia of Quantitative Finance |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/9780470061602.eqf13023 |access-date=2025-08-15 |publisher=John Wiley & Sons, Ltd |language=en |doi=10.1002/9780470061602.eqf13023 |isbn=978-0-470-06160-2|url-access=subscription }}</ref> The expansion expresses changes of a function of time and state variables over a small time interval in terms of a sum of multiple stochastic integrals involving derivatives of the function, [[Brownian motion]] integrals, [[Integral|time integrals]], and compensated Poisson integrals for jump components.

This expansion was first introduced by Wagner & Platen (1978) and was further refined in a series of foundational works, including Platen (1982b),<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Platen |first=E. |date=1982 |title=Ikeda, N. / Watanabe, S., Stochastic Differential Equations and Diffusion Processes. North-Holland Mathematical Library 24. Amsterdam-New York, North-Holland Publ. Co. 1981. 480 S., US $ 85.25. Dfl. 175.00. ISBN 0-444-86172-6 |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/zamm.19820621219 |journal=ZAMM - Journal of Applied Mathematics and Mechanics / Zeitschrift für Angewandte Mathematik und Mechanik |language=en |volume=62 |issue=12 |pages=713 |doi=10.1002/zamm.19820621219 |bibcode=1982ZaMM...62..713P |issn=1521-4001|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Platen & Wagner (1982), and the influential monograph Kloeden & Platen (1992).<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Kloeden |first1=Peter E. |last2=Platen |first2=Eckhard |date=1992 |title=Numerical Solution of Stochastic Differential Equations |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-662-12616-5 |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-3-662-12616-5 |isbn=978-3-642-08107-1 }}</ref>

The Wagner-Platen expansion provides the foundation of the numerical theory for stochastic differential equations, where it became truncated in appropriate ways to provide discrete-time approximations for solutions of [[stochastic]] differential equations, including the Euler-Maruyama scheme, the [[Milstein method|Milstein scheme]], and higher-order strong or weak schemes.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Papanicolaou |first=Andrew |date=2013-09-01 |title=Numerical Solution of Stochastic Differential Equations with Jumps in Finance |url=https://doi.org/10.1080/14697688.2013.828240 |journal=Quantitative Finance |volume=13 |issue=9 |pages=1353–1355 |doi=10.1080/14697688.2013.828240 |issn=1469-7688|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

===Benchmark approach===
Platen is the originator of the benchmark approach, a foundational alternative to [[Mathematical finance|classical mathematical finance.]]<ref name=opu/> Developed over decades, his theory replaces the traditional risk-neutral paradigm with a real-world pricing framework centered on the growth optimal portfolio (GOP).<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/advances-in-applied-probability/article/abs/arbitrage-in-continuous-complete-markets/90DC4B2C8DD7DC9B70864B1DD36F2879|title=Arbitrage in continuous complete markets|first=Eckhard|last=Platen|date=September 12, 2002|journal=Advances in Applied Probability|volume=34|issue=3|pages=540–558|doi=10.1239/aap/1033662165|url-access=subscription}}</ref> In his recent papers, Platen consolidates key results and applies the theory to long-term financial instruments, notably extreme-maturity zero-coupon bonds and European options.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1467-9965.2006.00265.x|title=A Benchmark Approach to Finance|first=Eckhard|last=Platen|date=January 12, 2006|journal=Mathematical Finance|volume=16|issue=1|pages=131–151|doi=10.1111/j.1467-9965.2006.00265.x|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/mafi.12065|title=Benchmarked Risk Minimization|first1=Ke|last1=Du|first2=Eckhard|last2=Platen|date=July 12, 2016|journal=Mathematical Finance|volume=26|issue=3|pages=617–637|doi=10.1111/mafi.12065|hdl=10453/36413|hdl-access=free|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022039604003262|title=Symmetry group methods for fundamental solutions|first1=Mark|last1=Craddock|first2=Eckhard|last2=Platen|date=December 15, 2004|journal=Journal of Differential Equations|volume=207|issue=2|pages=285–302|doi=10.1016/j.jde.2004.07.026|bibcode=2004JDE...207..285C |hdl=10453/3413|hdl-access=free|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite SSRN|last1=Eckhard |first1=Platen |title=Entropy-Maximizing Dynamics of Continuous Markets by Eckhard Platen |date=24 December 2023 |ssrn=4675048 }}</ref>

Platen first questioned classical pricing<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hofmann |first1=Norbert |last2=Platen |first2=Eckhard |last3=Schweizer |first3=Martin |date=1992 |title=Option Pricing Under Incompleteness and Stochastic Volatility |url=https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-9965.1992.tb00027.x |journal=Mathematical Finance |volume=2 |issue=3 |pages=153–187 |doi=10.1111/j.1467-9965.1992.tb00027.x |issn=0960-1627|url-access=subscription }}</ref> through early work on option pricing under [[stochastic volatility]], observing that risk-neutral prices for long-term contracts were systematically overpriced.<ref name=":1" /> This led him to formulate a model using the GOP—also known as the Kelly portfolio or numéraire portfolio as the central unit of value.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1467-9965.2008.00356.x|title=Consistent Market Extensions Under the Benchmark Approach|first1=Damir|last1=Filipović|first2=Eckhard|last2=Platen|date=January 12, 2009|journal=Mathematical Finance|volume=19|issue=1|pages=41–52 |doi=10.1111/j.1467-9965.2008.00356.x|url-access=subscription}}</ref> The GOP, which maximizes expected logarithmic utility, replaces the risk-free asset as numéraire and defines pricing under the real-world probability measure.<ref name="ddd" />

Platen shows that real-world pricing, which employs the GOP as the numéraire and the real-world probability measure as pricing measure, yields the lowest theoretically justifiable value for replicable contingent claims especially useful for valuing long-term contracts like pensions and insurance.<ref>https://www.arxiv.org/pdf/2506.16264

Pricing under the Benchmark Approach Eckhard Platen1,</ref>

Recognizing that the true GOP is difficult to implement due to high leverage, Platen introduced benchmark-neutral (BN) pricing in his 2024 work. This practical extension uses a well-diversified stock portfolio (excluding the savings account) as the numéraire. When the BN pricing measure is equivalent to the real-world one, BN prices match real-world prices.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Platen |first=Eckhard |date=2024 |title=Benchmark-Neutral Pricing |url=https://www.ssrn.com/abstract=4786090 |journal=SSRN Electronic Journal |language=en |doi=10.2139/ssrn.4786090 |issn=1556-5068}}</ref>

Platen applies the drifted time-transformed squared [[Bessel process]] of dimension four a key tool from his Minimal Market Model (MMM)—to approximate the GOP. His empirical results demonstrate that BN prices for extreme-maturity derivatives are significantly lower than their risk-neutral counterparts and can be accurately hedged, implying major cost savings in long-term finance.<ref name=":2">{{cite arXiv | last1=Platen | first1=Eckhard | title=Pricing under the Benchmark Approach | date=2025 | class=q-fin.MF | eprint=2506.16264 }}</ref>

Platen further grounds the benchmark approach in a broader scientific framework, involving information theory and using tools such as Li symmetry groups, information minimization, and Noether-type conservation laws.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Craddock |first1=Mark |last2=Platen |first2=Eckhard |date=2003-02-01 |title=Symmetry Group Methods for Fundamental Solutions and Characteristic Functions |url=https://ideas.repec.org//p/uts/rpaper/90.html |journal=Research Paper Series |language=en}}</ref>

The benchmark approach rests on two minimal assumptions: (1) the existence of the GOP, and (2) the minimization of the joint information of the risk-neutral pricing measure.<ref name=":2" /> The first assumption is less restrictive than those underpinning classical finance, notably avoiding the NFLVR condition.<ref>{{cite arXiv | last1=Platen | first1=Eckhard | title=Information-minimizing stationary financial market dynamics | date=2025 | class=q-fin.MF | eprint=2507.18395 }}</ref> Instead, the first assumption is equivalent to the No Unbounded Profit with Bounded Risk (NUPBR) condition by Karatzas and Kardaras.<ref name=":0" /> Platen argues, these two axioms allow much of financial market behavior to be derived, elevating finance to a discipline with predictive and explanatory depth comparable to the natural sciences.<ref name=":1" />
